mcqs.stem: Four options are given against each statement. Encircle the correct option. An outcome which represents how many times we expect the things to be happened is called:

mcqs.stem: Which one tells us how often a specific event occurs relative to the total number of frequency event or trials?
rationales: Expected frequency is the anticipated count of occurrences, not the proportion relative to all trials.
A sum of relative frequencies is an aggregate, not the frequency of one specific event relative to all trials.
Relative frequency is the number of occurrences of an event divided by the total number of trials.
Frequency is a count of occurrences and does not by itself give their proportion of all trials.

mcqs.stem: Estimated probability of an event occurring is also known as:
rationales: Relative frequency can be used to estimate the probability of an event.
Expected frequency is an anticipated count, not the estimated probability itself.
Class boundaries mark the limits of intervals in grouped data.
A sum of expected frequencies is a total count, not an estimated probability.

mcqs.stem: The sum of all expected frequencies is equal to the fixed number of:
rationales: Expected frequencies across all outcomes sum to the total number of trials.

Events are occurrences or sets of outcomes, not the fixed total number of trials.

mcqs.stem: The chance of occurrence of a particular event is called:
rationales: The sample space is the set of all possible outcomes, not the chance of an event.
Estimated probability is an approximation of that chance, whereas the general term asked for is probability.

Expected frequency is the anticipated number of occurrences, not the chance itself.

mcqs.stem: An event which will probably occur. It has greater chance to occur is called:
rationales: An equally likely event has the same chance as another event, rather than a greater chance.
A likely event has a greater chance of occurring than not occurring.
An unlikely event has a small chance of occurring.
A certain event is guaranteed to occur, rather than merely having a greater chance.

mcqs.stem: Find out the total number of possible sample space when 4 dice are rolled.:
rationales: Four dice have more than 6² possible ordered results.
Four dice have more than 6³ possible ordered results.
Each of the four dice has 6 possible results, giving 6⁴ outcomes in total.
6⁶ would count the outcomes for six dice, not four.

mcqs.stem: While rolling a pair of dice, what will be the probability of double 2?
rationales: A probability of 1/6 is too large because only one of 36 equally likely pairs is double 2.
A probability of 1/3 is too large because there is just one favorable pair.
A probability of 5/6 is the probability of not getting double 2, not of getting it.
Only the pair (2, 2) is double 2 among the 36 equally likely outcomes, so its probability is 1/36.

mcqs.stem: A card is chosen from a pack of 52 playing cards, find the probability of getting no jack and king:
rationales: There are 8 jacks and kings combined, so the probability of drawing one of them is 8/52, not 2/13.
There are 44 cards that are neither jacks nor kings, so the probability is 44/52 = 11/13.
2/52 is not the probability of drawing neither a jack nor a king; there are 44 such cards.
11/52 uses 11 as the number of favorable cards, but there are 44 cards that are neither jacks nor kings.
